correctness.rationale: At (1,1) the Jacobian is [[1,-1],[4,-3]] with trace -2, determinant 1. The modal determinant 1-(r-3)z+r z² has distinct roots for r>9 and trace stays negative; the r=9 double touch is treated separately. Isolated simple zero eigenvalues have nonzero derivative ±lambda sqrt((r-1)(r-9)), fulfilling simple-bifurcation transversality. Exact averaging of stationary nonlinearities yields means -7<UV>+3<V²>-3<U³> and -8<UV>+3<V²>-4<U³>; using first-order kernel vectors yields strictly negative quadratic coefficients for both populations. Strictly increasing simple path eigenvalues plus z+/z-→1 as r↓9 give arbitrarily many separated intervals. Symbolic and n≤40 graph computations reproduce algebra without being treated as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Quantifies a mathematically meaningful demographic consequence absent from linear network Turing tests: every locally bifurcating patterned stationary state in this model loses both prey and predator biomass, with exact positive coefficients and stronger predator reduction. An all-stationary-state mean-covariance/cubic identity provides a reproducible diagnostic beyond the local expansion. A sharp r=9 dispersal-ratio boundary and path graphs with unbounded numbers of disjoint stability-loss/return intervals make the effect testable at arbitrarily many distinct critical modes. Neither a parameter relabeling nor a finite table constitutes the essential assertion; stability of patterned branches and application to different kinetics are explicitly excluded.
